answer: The ferrous multiplier is published, charged in timber, and pearl lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 16 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, as the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 4576 identities would post 3089 proofs and burn roughly 36 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
